title: A fixed line total is removed when the work order becomes No Charge
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, in status Approved, with one approved line, line 1, with a Fixed Line Total of $1,250.00, 2.0 hours and one part costing $40.00.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Open the work order's three-dots menu.
  3. Click "Convert to No Charge".
  4. Pick "Goodwill" in Category.
  5. Click the confirming Convert to No Charge button.
  6. Open Edit Line on line 1.
  7. Open the Notes tab.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The menu shows "Convert to No Charge".

Step 3:

  • The confirmation opens.

Step 4:

  • Goodwill is picked.

Step 5:

  • Line 1 shows 2.0 hours and the part's cost $40.00 and no total.

Step 6:

  • The fixed-price fields are not shown in the line window.

Step 7:

  • The note records "Fixed line total $1,250.00 removed".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S2-R20: “Fixed price and Fixed Line Total: when a work order becomes internal or No Charge, or a line is marked No Charge, the line's fixed labor price and Fixed Line Total (labor and parts portions) are removed with the prices; cost and hours stay; the Labor + Parts = Total invariant is not checked on a line without a total; the note records what was removed ("Fixed line total $1,250.00 removed"). The fixed-price fields are hidden in the line dialog on such a line. Convert to Billable and Mark as Billable price the line as a new line (labor at rate, parts from the pricing rules on the cost), never restore the fixed amounts; the shop re-enters a fixed price if it wants one.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
